name: Non-Tiled 2D Gaussian Splatting with Transmittance Culling
definition: A rasterization method that iterates over Gaussians rather than tiles, using axis-aligned bounding boxes to limit pixel iteration and transmittance-based early ray termination for performance optimization.
summary: Non-Tiled 2D Gaussian Splatting with Transmittance Culling is a faster rasterization method that iterates over Gaussians rather than tiles, using transmittance-based early ray termination to skip fully opaque pixels.
